- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) or shows sharp reversal, model often overshoots downward; adjust downward bias or add early correction.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects or fails to revert; apply mean reversion bias toward prior 5-10 day average.
- When true outcome shows strong divergence from forecast (e.g., >5% error in first 3-5 days), model often fails to capture sentiment-driven volatility; reduce forecast smoothness or add sentiment-weighted volatility buffer.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.8 → -0.5 → +0.3), model tends to lag; adjust forecast horizon to align with sentiment momentum shift.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early in the horizon (first 5-7 days) when sentiment is bullish; apply early decay or downward bias for first 5 days if sentiment is fading.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.2), model tends to err on the side of overconfidence; reduce forecast magnitude by 2-5% unless sentiment is trending strongly.
